intended_object: The arrow outer(i) → inner(i) on arm i of the extended Dynkin quiver Ẽ₆, oriented towards the centre (three arms of length two). This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The quiver instance defines `Hom (outer i) (inner j)` as `PLift (i = j)`. So there is exactly one arrow from `outer i` to `inner i` and none from `outer i` to `inner j` when `j ≠ i`. Setting `outerArrow i := PLift.up rfl` picks out that single arrow, as the docstring says. This is a specific arrow of a specific quiver, so it cannot be too narrow, and Mathlib has no Ẽ₆ quiver to compare it with. The definition is correct and is the natural way to name this arrow.
